 Why Is Jamal Musiala Not Playing for Germany vs. Serbia?
 Originally posted on
 Athlon Sports 
  | 
 By Pragjyoti Singh
  | 
 Last updated Nov 13, 2026 2:50 PM ET
 Add us as a preferred source on Google
 Germany is without Jamal Musiala against Serbia today in the UEFA Nations League.
 They face Serbia in their fifth Group A2 fixture of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign at the Rajko Mitić Stadium in Belgrade.
 Jürgen Klopp’s side currently sits third in the group with five points from four matches, while Serbia is at the bottom without a point. The hosts have endured a difficult campaign, losing all four of their opening fixtures, and will be desperate to end that run in front of their home supporters.
 Germany, meanwhile, has struggled for consistency under Klopp. The former Liverpool boss has managed one win, two draws, and one loss across four matches, leaving them third in their group.
 Is Jamal Musiala Injured?
 Musiala is unavailable because of an injury and was not included in today’s squad. He is among several players missing from Klopp’s selection, with Serge Gnabry, Waldemar Anton, Assan Ouédraogo and Angelo Stiller also sidelined.
 Jamal Musiala takes a shot during the FIFA World Cup 2026 match between Germany and Cote D’Ivoire.Photo by Maciek Gudrymowicz/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images
 The Bayern Munich star’s absence is another setback for Germany, particularly given his ability to create chances and influence games in the attacking third. 
 Why Is Jamal Musiala Not Playing vs. Serbia?
 Musiala has been ruled out because of injury, meaning Klopp cannot call upon him for the Nations League encounter.
 The midfielder has been dealing with fitness problems during the international period and is not yet available to return to the national team. Jamal Musiala has been sidelined due to a muscle fiber tear sustained in September while warming up for Germany, alongside ongoing management of a neurological condition (absence seizures/dysfunction).
 The midfielder was previously diagnosed with temporary absence seizures that led to collapses during pre-season friendlies with Bayern Munich against RB Leipzig and Heidenheim.
